screen: btn/ai repeated on 28 boards inflates the edge matrix
finding: Thirteen percent of this section's wiring is one component instance repeated across 28 boards, all pointing at the same destination. It is the same counting artifact D-X-03 recorded for the rail, and it will distort any future graph analysis of the journey layer the same way.
recommend: Count component-instance reactions once per component, not once per instance, in any future edge analysis of this section — and note that the AI button is the ONLY control wired on most of these boards, which is how a section can look connected and be a slideshow (D-G-01).

screen: the publish gate is drawn on a black void
finding: The four boards that carry the product's most consequential decision — you may not publish yet — put a small modal on a 100%-opaque near-black rectangle named 'scrim', over an empty frame. Nothing is behind it. A designer cannot tell where the gate appears, and the renders read as a dark-theme product in a light-theme editor.
evidence: Measured on 307:2193, 307:2203, 307:2213: child RECTANGLE 'scrim', 1440x900 at 0,0, fill #111827, node opacity=1, fill opacity=1, visible=true. The frame's own fill is #f3f4f6 and the only other child is a 520x151 white card — 6.1% of the board. 131:201 has the same construction. DESIGN.md's editor chrome is the canonical light theme (dark-only was flipped 2026-04-18).
recommend: Put the editor behind the gate — 130:798 or 130:997 is the correct backdrop, since that is where the gate fires — and take the scrim to the token'd overlay alpha. On a board this important the surrounding state is the point: is Publish still visible, is the review pill still there, can the user reach the Review panel behind it.

screen: S1.4's three boards are 93% empty
finding: The setup checklist is drawn as three full 1440x900 frames each holding one 340x263 card on flat grey. There is no editor behind it, so the boards cannot show the one thing that matters about a floating checklist — what it covers.

On a real 1440 editor that card lands at x=1068-1408, which is inside the 300px inspector column (x=1140-1440) — no board shows that collision.

screen: the checklist's only interactive state has no board
finding: Every step in the shipped checklist expands to a description and a CTA button. No board in S1.4 draws an expanded step, so the checklist's only affordance is unspecified.

Boards 296:1972 / 296:1999 / 296:2030 draw seven bare checkbox rows and nothing else — 8-9 text nodes of chrome, no descriptions, no buttons. (The step LIST itself is correct: onboardingSteps.ts:31-34 cites board 296:1972 as its source, schema v5.)
recommend: Add one board: checklist with step 2 expanded, showing description + CTA. Also worth noting the collapsed pill: its boards 296:2064 and 296:2069 are in Archive, superseded by the footer band 1342:7162, so the collapse behaviour OnboardingMount.tsx:40 describes now has one board rather than two.

screen: the selection chip overlaps the customer's own site header
finding: On the 1440 editor boards the blue 'Section · Hero' selection label sits on top of the rendered site's brand text, so the first word of the customer's own header is unreadable.
evidence: 130:201: TEXT 'Bella Cucina' at y=209 x=428 (the canvas site header) and TEXT 'Section · Hero' at y=229 x=414 (the selection chip) — the chip's box starts 14px left of and 20px below the header text and covers it. Visible in the screenshots of 52:2, 130:201 and 130:400.

screen: MISSING JOURNEY — 'put it back the way it was'
finding: The most-used recovery job in any builder — I broke something, take me back — has screens but no journey. History and Compare each own panels; nothing in the file walks a user from a mistake to a restored site, and the two chords that start it are unboarded as entry points.
evidence: Editor-side and multi-step in code: VersionHistoryPanel.tsx:107,118-119,147-162,198-217,249-257 (restore-confirm band, in-flight VERSION_RESTORED listener, compare-on-expand, restore-failed toast); HistoryTab.tsx plus components/TimeTravelScrubber.tsx, SnapshotPreview.tsx, DiffRow.tsx, MilestoneSuggestionBanner.tsx, SavesChrome.tsx. Procedures siteVersion.create/list/get/delete (site-version.ts:24,33,40,47). Doors: SiteMenu.tsx:200 'Version history' and the ^H chord (useEditorShortcuts.ts:124). Publish-side rollback is a second chain: sites.publishHistory/publishDiff/rollback (sites.ts:451,466,481), PublishHistory.tsx:101-105,122-134,181-219 with an ADMIN gate at :104. Journeys has no S-number for any of it.
recommend: Add an S-flow: notice the mistake → open history (^H) → compare → restore-confirm → restoring → restored, with the failure branch and the ADMIN-blocked branch. The screens mostly exist in History (162:2, 163:167, 184:2, 184:24, 184:37, 184:45, 453:4064); what is missing is the walk that proves they connect.

screen: MISSING JOURNEY — 'let my client see it before it goes live'
finding: S4.1 share-preview is already known to have no board. Grounded against code it is worse than a missing screen: it is a shipping, plan-gated, eight-state journey with a door in the editor's own Site menu and a public route, and the only description of it anywhere is a caption.
evidence: Caption 817:4855 in Notes carries a 5-feature spec (copy link, expiry 24h/7d/30d/Never, password toggle, QR, email invite) and its own name says NO BOARD ANYWHERE. Code: siteDetail.sharing.list/create/revoke (site-detail.ts:309,322,357); share-link.service.ts:12-79 — bcrypt password, expiresInDays capped by plan, password itself plan-gated (allowPasswords), revoke; public route packages/dashboard/app/share/[token]/page.tsx; editor door SiteMenu.tsx:276 'Share preview link' → /dashboard/sites/{id}?share=1. Distinct from /review/[token], which is S5.
recommend: Board it: no links → create (expiry + password) → plan-blocked variant → created + copy → revoke confirm → visitor's password gate → expired link. Note the hand-off is itself a design question — the editor's menu row leaves the editor, which is the same shape as the activity-log split in D-G-13.

screen: MISSING JOURNEY — 'the AI wants to publish my site'
finding: A shipping gate lets an AI agent propose a privileged action — publishing — which the user must confirm within five minutes, once. It has no board, and its natural home was S2, which is retired. Nothing in the file shows a user being asked to approve something an agent wants to do.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/sidebar/tabs/ai/hooks/useAiActionGate.ts:10-12 'The AI privileged-action confirm gate (platform phase 4b). An AI propose-action… Confirm exports the pages, calls actions.confirm (which re-checks the role…)'; :44 actions.propose.mutate, :69 actions.confirm.mutate. server/services/action-confirmation.service.ts:1-11 — single-use grants, TTL_MS = 5 minutes, confirm consumes the row atomically and requires the session actor to match the proposer. AITab.tsx:186 routes the proposal; useAgentRunner.ts:69 routes mid-run proposals. exportPublishPages.ts:12-14 confirms this path and the Topbar publish button must produce identical pages. Full-file name sweep: no board matches; 170:97 'AI · step-gate' is the per-step apply gate inside an agent run, a different object.
recommend: Board the confirm: what the agent is asking for, what will go live, who is asking, the countdown, and the refusal. This is the only place in the product where software asks permission to change the customer's public site — it should not be the only one with no design.

screen: MISSING JOURNEY — 'someone else changed this while I had it open'
finding: S1 covers crash-recovery, load-error, offline and force-refresh but not the one save failure that makes the user choose. The conflict modal is a three-branch decision with a second confirm behind the destructive branch, and it has no journey board.
evidence: packages/editor/src/editor/shell/modals/ConflictModal.tsx:1-18,34-36 — three branches (Reload latest · Save a backup then reload · Overwrite) plus a confirmOverwrite gate. The Shell module has 66:640 'Shell state 11 · Saving → conflict', which is the banner, not the decision. S1's boards are 297:2027 crash-recovery, 297:2139 load-error, 807:7000 offline-restored, 813:4888 force-refresh, 813:4836 save-indicator — none of them draws a choice.
recommend: Add it to S1: conflict → the three branches → overwrite-confirm → each outcome, including overwrite-failed. This is a data-loss decision made under time pressure and it is currently specified only in a component file.
